en: 1 piece of sangak or lavash bread
50 g low-salt white cheese
Fresh herbs (mint, basil, tarragon)
5 walnut halves
Cucumber and tomato slices
Warm the bread briefly until it softens
Arrange the cheese and walnuts on a plate
Wash and dry the herbs and set them alongside
Wrap a bite of bread around cheese and a herb sprig
2 eggs
3 ripe tomatoes
1 tsp oil
A pinch of turmeric
Salt and black pepper
Peel the tomatoes and chop them small
Heat the oil, add the turmeric, then the tomatoes
Cook 10 minutes until the water evaporates
Crack in the eggs and stir gently until just set
2 eggs
Chopped parsley, coriander and dill 50 g (mixed herbs)
2 tbsp chopped spring onion
Coarsely chopped walnuts 10 g and a few barberries (optional)
Turmeric, salt and black pepper
1 tsp oil
Beat the eggs with the salt, black pepper and turmeric.
Add the chopped herbs, spring onion and walnuts and mix well until the batter is dense with herbs.
Heat the oil in a small pan over low heat, pour in the mixture and spread it out.
Cover and cook 8-10 minutes until the surface sets, then flip and cook 3-4 minutes more, garnishing with barberries if using.

name.en: Nimru (Persian Turmeric Fried Eggs) with Bread

en: 2 eggs
1 tsp oil or butter
Turmeric, salt and black pepper
1 slice whole-wheat bread (40 g)
1 small tomato, sliced (traditional, optional)
Ground dried mint for garnish
Heat the oil in a small pan over low heat and add the turmeric until fragrant and the oil turns golden.
If using tomato, fry it for 2 minutes first until slightly softened.
Crack the eggs into the coloured oil and let them cook gently until the whites set and the yolks stay soft.
Sprinkle with salt, black pepper and dried mint, and serve immediately with the bread.

name.en: Persian Halim (Wheat and Chicken Porridge with Cinnamon)

en: Broken wheat 40 g
Boiled, shredded chicken breast 60 g
1 small onion
Garlic paste, turmeric and salt
1 tsp ghee
Ground cinnamon and a light dusting of sugar for garnish
Boil the broken wheat in plenty of water until fully dissolved (25-30 minutes), whisk into a smooth porridge.
Brown the onion in the ghee, add the garlic paste and turmeric and stir for a minute.
Add the shredded chicken and this mixture to the porridge and stir over low heat 5 minutes until combined.
Add salt, pour into a serving bowl, and sprinkle cinnamon and a little sugar on top.

name.en: Sangak Flatbread with Walnut and Herb Spread

en: Whole-wheat flatbread, 1 piece (60 g) as a sangak substitute
Ground walnuts 25 g
1 tbsp low-fat yogurt
Finely chopped parsley and mint
1 small crushed garlic clove and salt
1 tsp olive oil
Grind the walnuts with the yogurt, garlic and salt into a thick paste.
Add the chopped parsley and mint and mix well.
Warm the bread briefly on a dry griddle or in the oven.
Spread the walnut paste on the bread, drizzle with olive oil, and serve immediately.

name.en: Halva Ardeh (Sesame Paste Spread) with Bread

en: Sesame paste (tahini) 30 g
Date syrup or honey 2 tsp
1 slice whole-wheat bread (40 g)
Coarsely chopped walnuts 10 g
A pinch of ground cinnamon
Warm water as needed to loosen the texture
Mix the tahini with the date syrup or honey thoroughly.
Add warm water a spoonful at a time until the texture spreads easily.
Spread it on the bread and sprinkle the chopped walnuts and cinnamon on top.
Serve immediately, with a cup of tea if desired.
2 eggs
Low-fat feta cheese, crumbled, 30 g
Coarsely chopped walnuts 15 g
1 tbsp chopped spring onion
Black pepper and a little salt (feta is already salty)
1 tsp oil
Beat the eggs with the black pepper and a little salt.
Add the crumbled feta, walnuts and spring onion and mix gently.
Heat the oil in a small pan over medium heat, pour in the mixture.
Cook 3-4 minutes until the bottom sets, fold in half, cook 1 more minute, and serve hot.
Pearl barley 40 g
1 medium onion and garlic paste
Chopped herbs (parsley, dill) 40 g
Low-fat yogurt 60 g
1 tsp oil, turmeric and salt
Dried mint for garnish
Soak the barley for an hour, then boil in plenty of water 30-35 minutes until soft.
Heat the oil and brown the onion, add the garlic paste and turmeric and stir for a minute.
Add the onion and chopped herbs to the boiled barley and cook 10 minutes more.
Add salt, pour into a serving bowl, and top with the yogurt and dried mint.

name.en: Persian Scrambled Eggs with Tomato and Pepper

en: 2 eggs
1 medium tomato, chopped
Chopped green bell pepper
1 small onion
Turmeric, salt and black pepper
1 tsp oil, and 1 slice whole-wheat bread (30 g)
Heat the oil and sauté the onion until softened, add the bell pepper and stir for two minutes.
Add the tomato and turmeric and cook until the tomato softens and loses its excess water.
Beat the eggs with salt and black pepper and pour into the pan.
Stir constantly until the eggs set and become crumbly, and serve with the bread.
150 g chicken breast
120 g cooked basmati rice
2 tbsp barberries (zereshk)
Saffron threads, steeped
1 onion, 1 tsp oil, cinnamon
Sauté the onion, then add the chicken, cinnamon and half a cup of water
Cook 25 minutes until done with a little sauce left
Rinse the barberries and toast them for one minute only
Mix a spoon of saffron into the rice, serve with chicken and barberries
120 g brown lentils
1 onion, 2 garlic cloves
1 tsp tomato paste
Turmeric, cinnamon, cumin
1 tsp oil, lemon juice
Soak the lentils an hour and drain them
Sauté the onion and garlic with the turmeric
Add the tomato paste, lentils and 3 cups of water
Simmer 35 minutes, finish with cinnamon and lemon juice

name.en: Ghormeh Sabzi with Beef and Kidney Beans, with Rice

en: Lean beef, cubed, 100 g
Cooked red kidney beans 40 g
Cooked basmati rice 120 g
Chopped herbs (parsley, coriander, fenugreek leaves) 80 g
1 medium onion and 2 dried limes
1 tsp oil, turmeric and salt
Heat the oil and stir the chopped herbs over medium heat for 10 minutes until they lose their moisture and turn deep green.
In a separate pot, brown the onion, add the beef and turmeric and stir until it changes colour.
Add the cooked herbs, beans, one and a half cups of water and the pierced dried limes, cover and simmer 50-60 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add salt, and press the limes lightly with a spoon to release their flavour, then serve over the rice.

name.en: Chicken Fesenjan with Walnuts and Pomegranate, with Rice

en: Chicken breast pieces 130 g
Cooked basmati rice 110 g
Ground walnuts 40 g
Pomegranate paste (unsweetened) 2 tbsp
1 medium onion
1 tsp oil, turmeric, cinnamon, salt and a little sugar to taste if needed
Brown the onion in the oil until golden, add the turmeric and chicken and stir until it changes colour.
Add the ground walnuts and a cup of water and stir well until the walnuts dissolve into the liquid.
Add the pomegranate paste and cinnamon, cover and simmer on very low heat 40-45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the chicken is tender.
Add salt and adjust the sweetness with a little sugar if the sauce is too tart, then serve over the rice.

name.en: Baghali Polo with Chicken (Dill Rice with Fava Beans)

en: Chicken breast pieces 130 g
Basmati rice 100 g
Cooked fava beans 40 g (or lima beans as a substitute)
Fresh dill, chopped, 30 g
Garlic-ginger paste and turmeric
2 tsp oil and salt
Season the chicken with the garlic-ginger paste, turmeric and salt and let it sit 15 minutes.
Heat the oil and cook the chicken 8-10 minutes until fully done, set aside.
Boil the rice to 70 percent doneness, add the fava beans and dill and mix gently.
Layer the rice into a greased pot, cover and cook on very low heat 20 minutes until a crisp bottom forms, and serve with the chicken.

name.en: Loobia Polo (Green Bean and Meat Rice)

en: Lean minced beef 100 g
Fresh green beans, chopped, 150 g
Basmati rice 100 g
1 medium onion and puréed tomato 60 g
Cinnamon, turmeric and salt
2 tsp oil
Brown the onion in the oil, add the minced meat and turmeric and stir until it changes colour.
Add the green beans, tomato and cinnamon, cover and cook 15 minutes until the beans soften.
Boil the rice to 70 percent doneness.
Layer the rice with the meat and bean mixture in a greased pot, cover and cook on very low heat 20 minutes, and serve hot.

name.en: Ash-e Reshteh (Persian Herb, Bean and Noodle Soup)

en: Thin vermicelli or broken noodles 40 g
Cooked red kidney beans and chickpeas 60 g
Chopped herbs (spinach, parsley, coriander, dill) 100 g
1 medium onion and garlic paste
2 tbsp low-fat yogurt (a kashk substitute)
1 tsp oil, turmeric, salt and dried mint
Brown the onion in the oil, add the garlic paste and turmeric and stir for a minute.
Add the chopped herbs and stir for 5 minutes until wilted.
Add the beans, chickpeas and three cups of water, cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Add the vermicelli and salt and cook 10 minutes more, pour into serving bowls and top with the yogurt and dried mint.

name.en: Adas Polo ba Goosht (Lentil Rice with Meat)

en: Lean minced beef 100 g
Cooked brown lentils 40 g
Basmati rice 100 g
1 medium onion and raisins 15 g
Cinnamon, turmeric and salt
2 tsp oil
Brown the onion in the oil until golden, set half aside for garnish.
Add the minced meat and turmeric to the remaining onion and stir until it changes colour.
Boil the rice to 70 percent doneness, add the cooked lentils and cinnamon and mix gently.
Layer the rice with the meat mixture in a greased pot, cover and cook on very low heat 20 minutes, and garnish with the fried onion and raisins.

name.en: Ash-e Reshteh-ye Morgh (Persian Chicken and Chickpea Noodle Soup)

en: Chicken breast, small pieces, 100 g
Thin vermicelli or broken noodles 30 g
Cooked chickpeas 50 g
1 medium onion and garlic paste
Chopped herbs (parsley, coriander) 60 g
1 tsp oil, turmeric and salt
Brown the onion in the oil, add the garlic paste, turmeric and chicken and stir until it changes colour.
Add the chopped herbs and stir 5 minutes until wilted.
Add the chickpeas and three cups of water, cover and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the vermicelli and salt and cook 10 minutes more until the chicken is fully cooked, and serve hot.

name.en: Sabzi Polo with Fish (Herb Rice with Fish)

en: White fish fillet 140 g
Basmati rice 100 g
Chopped herbs (dill, parsley, coriander) 100 g
2 crushed garlic cloves and turmeric
Lemon juice and salt
2 tsp oil
Season the fish with the crushed garlic, turmeric, lemon juice and salt, let it sit 15 minutes.
Heat one teaspoon of oil and cook the fish 3-4 minutes per side until done, set aside.
Boil the rice to 70 percent doneness, add the chopped herbs and mix gently.
Put the rice in a pot greased with the remaining oil, cover and cook on very low heat 20 minutes, and serve with the fish.
170 g chicken, cubed
3 tbsp yogurt
Saffron threads in warm water
Juice of half a lemon, 1 grated onion
1 tsp oil, salt, pepper
Mix the yogurt, saffron, lemon, onion and oil
Marinate the chicken and chill at least 4 hours
Thread it onto the skewers
Grill 12 minutes, turning and brushing with saffron water
120 g lean lamb, cubed
2 medium aubergines
1 onion and 2 tomatoes
1 tsp tomato paste, turmeric
1 tbsp oil, sour grapes or lemon
Slice the aubergines and salt them for 30 minutes
Brown the onion, then the meat with the turmeric
Add the tomato paste and 2 cups of water, cook 45 minutes
Roast the aubergine in the oven and lay it on top for 10 minutes

name.en: Grilled Kabab Koobideh with Shirazi Salad

en: Lean minced beef 150 g
1 medium onion, grated and squeezed of its liquid
1 tsp turmeric, salt and black pepper
Tomato, cucumber and red onion, finely chopped, for the salad
Lemon juice and 1 tsp oil for the salad
Saffron strands for garnish (optional)
Knead the minced meat with the squeezed onion, turmeric, salt and black pepper thoroughly until it binds and becomes tacky (the key to good koobideh is thorough kneading).
Wet your hands and shape the meat around a flat skewer, pressing with your fingers to form ridges.
Grill over very hot coals or a griddle pan 8-10 minutes, turning, until fully cooked with charred spots.
Mix the salad ingredients with lemon juice and oil, and serve with the kabab.

name.en: Khoresh Gheimeh (Split Pea and Meat Stew with Dried Lime) with Rice

en: Beef, small cubes, 100 g
Cooked split yellow peas 40 g
Cooked basmati rice 110 g
Puréed tomato 80 g and 1 medium onion
2 pierced dried limes
Garlic paste, turmeric, cinnamon, salt and 1 tsp oil
Brown the onion in the oil, add the garlic paste, turmeric and beef and stir until it changes colour.
Add the tomato and cook 5 minutes, then add a cup of water, the dried limes and cinnamon.
Cover and simmer 45 minutes until the beef is tender, then add the cooked split peas and salt and cook 10 minutes more.
Press the limes lightly to release their flavour, then serve over the rice.

name.en: Khoresh Karafs (Celery and Herb Stew with Meat) with Rice

en: Beef, small cubes, 100 g
Chopped celery 150 g
Cooked basmati rice 110 g
Chopped parsley and mint 60 g
1 medium onion and garlic paste
1 tsp oil, turmeric and fresh lemon to serve
Heat the oil and stir the parsley and mint over medium heat 5 minutes until they lose their moisture.
In a separate pot, brown the onion, add the meat, garlic paste and turmeric and stir until it changes colour.
Add the cooked herbs and celery and a cup of water, cover and simmer 40-45 minutes until the meat is tender and the celery softens.
Adjust the salt, and serve over the rice with fresh lemon slices.

name.en: Tahchin (Baked Saffron Rice Cake with Chicken)

en: Boiled, shredded chicken breast 100 g
Basmati rice 100 g
Low-fat yogurt 60 g
Saffron strands soaked in 2 tbsp warm water
1 egg
1 tsp oil, salt and barberries for garnish (optional)
Boil the rice to 70 percent doneness, drain.
Beat the egg with the yogurt, saffron water and salt.
Mix two thirds of the rice with the yogurt mixture, leaving the remaining third plain.

Grease an oven-safe dish, layer the yogurt rice, then the chicken, then the remaining rice, press down firmly, cover with foil and bake at 180°C for 45-50 minutes until a golden crust forms on the bottom, then invert onto a serving plate.

name.en: Khoresh Rivas (Rhubarb and Herb Stew with Meat) with Rice

en: Beef, small cubes, 100 g
Chopped rhubarb 100 g (or a substitute sour vegetable like chard with lemon juice)
Chopped parsley and mint 60 g
Cooked basmati rice 110 g
1 medium onion, garlic paste and turmeric
1 tsp oil, salt and a little sugar to balance the tartness
Heat the oil and stir the parsley and mint over medium heat 5 minutes until they lose their moisture.
In a separate pot, brown the onion, add the meat, garlic paste and turmeric and stir until it changes colour.
Add the cooked herbs and a cup of water, cover and simmer 35 minutes until the meat is tender.
Add the rhubarb, salt and a little sugar, cook 10 minutes more until the rhubarb softens without fully dissolving, and serve over the rice.
Thin beef slices (fillet or tenderloin) 150 g
1 medium onion, grated
Saffron strands soaked in 2 tbsp warm water
Lemon juice and 1 tsp olive oil
Salt and black pepper
Cherry tomatoes for grilling (optional)
Mix the grated onion with the saffron water, lemon juice, oil, salt and black pepper.
Marinate the beef slices in the mixture and chill for at least 45 minutes.
Thread onto flat skewers, folding slightly, and grill over very hot coals or a griddle pan 5-6 minutes, turning.
Grill the cherry tomatoes alongside if desired, and serve the kabab immediately.

name.en: Morasa Polo ba Morgh (Persian Jeweled Rice with Chicken)

en: Chicken breast pieces 130 g
Basmati rice 100 g
Grated carrot, thin strips, 40 g
Dried barberries and raisins 15 g
Grated orange zest and saffron strands
2 tsp oil, cinnamon and salt
Season the chicken with salt and cinnamon, heat a teaspoon of oil and cook it 8-10 minutes until fully done, set aside.
Sauté the carrot with a little sugar and water for 5 minutes until tender, then add the barberries, raisins and orange zest and stir for two minutes.
Boil the rice to 70 percent doneness.
Layer the rice into a greased pot, then the carrot mixture, then the remaining rice, cover and cook on very low heat 20 minutes, and serve with the chicken.
Lean minced beef 100 g
Chopped cabbage 150 g
Basmati rice 100 g
1 medium onion and garlic paste
Dried mint, cinnamon, turmeric and salt
2 tsp oil
Knead the minced meat with half the grated onion, salt and cinnamon, shape into very small balls.
Heat the oil and cook the meatballs 6-7 minutes, turning, until done, set aside.
In the same pan, sauté the cabbage with the remaining onion, garlic and turmeric 7-8 minutes until it softens.
Boil the rice to 70 percent doneness, layer it with the cabbage and meatballs in a greased pot, cover and cook on very low heat 20 minutes.
150 g plain yogurt
1 cucumber, grated and squeezed
1 tsp dried mint
1 tbsp crushed walnuts
Salt, raisins (optional)
Grate the cucumber and squeeze out the water well
Mix it with the yogurt, salt and dried mint
Chill 20 minutes in the fridge
Top with the walnuts and raisins before serving
10 g pistachios
10 g almonds and walnuts
5 g dried mulberries
5 g dried apricot, chopped
A pinch of salt (optional)
Toast the nuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes
Let them cool completely
Mix them with the dried fruit
Keep in an airtight jar and eat a measured handful
Medium aubergine 200 g
Low-fat yogurt 60 g (a whey substitute)
1 small onion, sliced and fried
Dried mint and crushed garlic
1 tsp oil and salt
Coarsely chopped walnuts 8 g for garnish
Roast the aubergine directly over a flame or in the oven until the skin chars and the flesh is soft, then peel and mash it.
Heat the oil and brown half the onion with the garlic, add the mashed aubergine and salt and cook 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the yogurt and dried mint, mixing well.
Pour into a serving dish, garnish with the remaining fried onion and walnuts, and serve with bread.

name.en: Borani Esfenaj (Spinach Yogurt Dip with Garlic)

en: Fresh spinach, chopped, 150 g
Low-fat yogurt 100 g
2 crushed garlic cloves
1 tsp oil
Dried mint and salt
Chopped walnuts for garnish (optional)
Boil the spinach in a little water for 3-4 minutes until wilted, drain and squeeze out the excess water well.
Heat the oil and gently brown the garlic until fragrant without burning.
Mix the drained spinach with the garlic, yogurt, dried mint and salt.
Chill for half an hour, garnish with walnuts if desired, and serve with bread.

name.en: Mast-o Musir (Yogurt with Dried Wild Shallot)

en: Low-fat yogurt 150 g
Finely chopped spring onion, 2 tbsp (a wild shallot substitute)
Ground dried mint
Salt and a little lemon juice
1 tsp olive oil for garnish
Whisk the yogurt until smooth.
Add the chopped spring onion, dried mint and salt and stir well.
Add a little lemon juice and mix.
Chill for 15 minutes, drizzle with olive oil on top, and serve with bread.
Grated zucchini, squeezed of liquid, 200 g
1 egg
2 tbsp whole-wheat flour
Chopped spring onion and turmeric
Salt and black pepper
1 tsp oil for brushing
Mix the squeezed zucchini with the egg, flour, spring onion, turmeric, salt and black pepper until well combined.
Spoon the mixture into small flat mounds on a lined tray.
Brush the tops with oil.
Bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden.
Low-fat yogurt 150 g
Coarsely ground walnuts 25 g
1 very small crushed garlic clove
Dried mint and salt
A few drops of rosewater (optional)
Wild thyme or fresh mint for garnish
Whisk the yogurt until smooth.
Add the ground walnuts, crushed garlic, dried mint and salt and mix well.
Add a few drops of rosewater if desired.
Chill for 15 minutes, garnish with wild thyme or fresh mint, and serve with bread.
Boiled mashed potato 150 g
1 egg
Chopped spring onion and turmeric
Salt and black pepper
1 tbsp whole-wheat flour
1 tsp oil for brushing
Mix the mashed potato with the egg, spring onion, turmeric, salt, black pepper and flour until well combined.
Spoon the mixture into small flat mounds on a lined tray.
Brush the tops with oil.
Bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden.

name.en: Panir Sabzi Roll (Feta and Herb Wrap)

en: Thin whole-wheat flatbread, 1 piece (50 g)
Low-fat feta cheese, crumbled, 40 g
Chopped herbs (fresh mint, parsley, basil) 40 g
Chopped walnuts 10 g
Thinly sliced cucumber and tomato
A light squeeze of lemon juice
Warm the bread briefly on a dry griddle to make it pliable.
Spread the crumbled feta over the bread.
Arrange the herbs, walnuts, cucumber and tomato on top, and drizzle with lemon juice.
Roll the bread tightly and cut in half, and serve immediately.
Cooked, mashed brown lentils 150 g
1 egg
Chopped spring onion and turmeric
Chopped herbs (parsley) 1 tbsp
Salt, black pepper and 1 tbsp whole-wheat flour
1 tsp oil for brushing
Mix the mashed lentils with the egg, spring onion, turmeric, parsley, salt, black pepper and flour until well combined.
Shape the mixture into small flat patties with your hands.
Arrange them on a lined tray and brush both sides with oil.
Bake at 220°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.
50 g cooked thin rice vermicelli
1 cup water
1 tsp sugar or honey
1 tsp rose water
Juice of 1 lime, lime slices
Mix the water with the sugar and rose water, then chill
Cut the cooked vermicelli into short pieces
Combine with the liquid and freeze 2 hours
Scrape with a fork and serve with the lime juice
150 g Greek yogurt
Half cup pomegranate seeds
1 tbsp crushed pistachios
1 tsp honey
A few drops of rose water
Stir the yogurt with the honey and rose water
Spoon half of it into a cup
Add half the pomegranate seeds, then the rest of the yogurt
Top with pomegranate and pistachios, serve chilled

name.en: Sholeh Zard (Saffron and Cinnamon Rice Pudding)

en: Basmati rice 40 g
Water 250 ml and low-fat milk 100 ml
Sugar 25 g
Saffron strands soaked in 2 tbsp warm water
1 tsp ghee and ground cinnamon
Chopped almonds and pistachios 8 g for garnish
Boil the rice in the water over medium heat 20 minutes until it fully breaks down into a near-mush.
Add the milk and continue cooking over low heat 10 minutes, stirring, until the texture thickens.
Add the sugar, saffron water and ghee, and cook 8-10 minutes more, stirring, until it becomes thick and glossy.
Pour into serving bowls, sprinkle with cinnamon and nuts, and serve warm or chilled.

name.en: Persian Baghlava with Rosewater and Pistachios

en: Filo pastry, 4 sheets (60 g)
Coarsely ground pistachios 40 g
Sugar 15 g and ground cardamom
2 tsp melted ghee for brushing
1 tsp rosewater, sugar 10 g and water 30 ml for a light syrup
Saffron strands (optional)
Mix the ground pistachios with the sugar and cardamom.
Lay out a sheet of filo and brush with ghee, add a layer of the pistachio mixture, repeat the layers until the sheets run out.
Cut the pastry into small diamonds before baking, bake at 180°C for 15-18 minutes until golden and crisp.
Boil the rosewater, sugar and water for two minutes into a light syrup, pour it over the hot baghlava right after baking, and let it cool before serving.
Whole-wheat flour 40 g and 1 tbsp cornflour
2 tbsp yogurt and a pinch of baking soda
Saffron strands soaked in 2 tbsp warm water
Sugar 25 g, water 30 ml and a little lemon juice for a light syrup
1 tsp rosewater
1 tsp oil for brushing
Mix the flour and cornflour with the yogurt, baking soda and saffron water into a thick, pipeable batter (like a thick pancake batter).
Put it in a piping bag or a plastic bag with a corner cut off, and pipe small rings onto a lined tray.
Brush with oil and bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes until golden.
Boil the sugar, water and lemon juice for two minutes, add the rosewater, and pour it over the hot rings right out of the oven.
Rice flour 50 g
Icing sugar 15 g
2 tsp melted ghee
1 tbsp yogurt
Ground cardamom and saffron strands soaked in half a tsp water
Poppy seeds or ground pistachios for garnish (optional)
Mix the melted ghee with the icing sugar until creamy.
Add the yogurt, soaked saffron and cardamom and mix.
Gradually add the rice flour and knead gently until you get a soft, non-sticky dough.
Shape into small flat balls, sprinkle with poppy seeds if desired, and bake at 160°C for 15-18 minutes until the edges firm up without much colouring, let cool completely before serving.
Chickpea flour (besan) 50 g
Icing sugar 15 g
2 tsp melted ghee
Ground cardamom
A pinch of cinnamon
Ground pistachios for garnish (optional)
Toast the chickpea flour in a dry pan over low heat 5-6 minutes, stirring constantly, until it smells toasted and turns light golden.
Let it cool slightly, then mix with the melted ghee, icing sugar, cardamom and cinnamon until it comes together.
Shape into small flat balls or use a mould for a star shape.
Arrange on a lined tray, sprinkle with pistachios if desired, and let them air-dry 30 minutes or bake at 150°C for just 8-10 minutes without colouring, then cool completely before serving.
Cornflour 30 g
Water 200 ml
Sugar 20 g
Saffron strands soaked in 2 tbsp warm water
1 tsp rosewater
Chopped pistachios and almonds 8 g for garnish
Dissolve the cornflour in half a cup of cold water until completely lump-free.
Heat the remaining water with the sugar until it boils, then gradually stir in the cornflour mixture over low heat, stirring constantly.
Add the saffron water and keep stirring 5-6 minutes until the texture becomes translucent and jelly-thick.
Remove from the heat and add the rosewater, pour into small dishes, chill for two hours until set, and garnish with the nuts before serving.
Pitted dates 150 g
Whole walnuts for stuffing the dates 30 g
Whole-wheat flour 25 g
1 tsp ghee for the toasted mixture
Ground cinnamon and ground cardamom
Ground pistachios for garnish
Stuff each date with half a walnut, arrange them in a single layer on a serving dish.
Heat the ghee and toast the flour over low heat 4-5 minutes, stirring constantly, until it turns golden and fragrant.
Add the cinnamon and cardamom and keep stirring for a minute.
Sprinkle the toasted flour mixture evenly over the stuffed dates, sprinkle with pistachios, and chill for half an hour before serving.
Fine semolina 40 g
Whole-wheat flour 15 g
Icing sugar 15 g
2 tsp melted ghee
Saffron strands soaked in 1 tbsp warm water
Ground cardamom and poppy seeds for garnish (optional)
Toast the semolina and flour together in a dry pan over low heat 6-7 minutes, stirring constantly, until they turn light golden and fragrant.
Let them cool slightly, then mix with the melted ghee, icing sugar, saffron water and cardamom until a soft dough forms.
Shape into small flat balls or use a mould to form them.
Arrange on a lined tray, sprinkle with poppy seeds if desired, and bake at 160°C for 12-15 minutes until the edges firm up without much colouring, let cool completely before serving.
